correctness.rationale: Every mixed independent class is a unique matched L_i,R_i pair. The remaining index set U gives pure-shore classes, and if U is empty the matched pairs cannot be distinguished. In a common pure left class, two vertices at indices i,j differ in either code exactly when one of their matched right endpoints is a singleton: all other pure left classes are at distance two from both, mixed classes at one, and a nonsingleton pure right class at one. A matched right singleton has distances three and one, respectively, contributing precisely the missing neighbor color. The argument is symmetric on the other shore. Same-colored matched vertices with U nonempty are distinguished by any pure left class (distances two and one and adjacency only on one side). This proves equivalence for every proper coloring. If there are p mixed classes and m=n-p residual indices, and r singleton and t nonsingleton right classes, each left class contains at most one of the m-r indices in nonsingleton right classes. Thus for t>=1 there are at least p+(m-r)+r+t>=n+1 classes; if t=0, the m right singletons and at least one pure left class give the same lower bound. The single pure left class and all right singletons show attainability. At equality with t>=1, t=1 and every left class has one index of the right block B. Symmetry permits at most one of those left classes to be nonsingleton, so all of U minus B join that class if the set is nonempty. This gives exactly the one-shore or two-block forms, with the one-index case counted only once. For fixed m this counts m*2^(m-1)-2m+2 partitions without names; binomial summation gives n*3^(n-1)-(n-2)*2^n-2. An independent proper-partition enumeration for n=3–6 found 41, 354, 4,125, 61,375 proper partitions and 17, 74, 307, 1,200 optima, respectively, with no discrepancies between the two coloring tests. That enumeration corroborates only the finite orders; the supplied programs were inspected, not executed.

evidence: For twin-free graphs the Alcón et al. upper bound is |V|-alpha+1. In the crown alpha=n because any mixed independent set has size at most two and each shore has size n.
Chakraborty et al. discuss both parameters and equality in other bipartite examples, including a star. Behtoei's inspected results are for joins and complete multipartite graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The twin-free theorem indeed gives n+1 as an upper bound; neither it nor those inspected relationships establishes a matching lower bound, a per-partition equivalence, or rigidity. The star result concerns a different bipartite graph.

evidence: The general inequality and the known upper bound tell only one side of the optimum. The new counting identity depends on every optimum having at most one nonsingleton pure block per shore and a single common index if both are present.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Even an equality of the two minima would not imply that the sets of proper partitions satisfying the two conditions coincide. The prior upper bound and different enumerator conditions do not supply that set equivalence or the classification at equality.

evidence: The crown is the direct (categorical) product K_n times K_2, not any of the products listed in the 2024 product paper's abstract. Missing cross edges are a perfect matching; for n>=3 the graph is not a complete multipartite join.
Resultary 611f26de2ae5 uses matching-deleted bicliques but requires proper conflict-free coloring; 625010bcb3e9 uses crowns but requires that proper colorings break automorphisms.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Same graph, or even a count of proper partitions of it, is not an equivalent coloring problem unless the additional constraint is the same. Conflict-free and symmetry-breaking constraints are different from separation of same-color vertices by color-neighborhood or metric codes.

value.rationale: These two separation notions can differ on general graphs. On a natural dense bipartite family, the theorem identifies which geometric obstructions make the notions agree, characterizes every optimum rather than giving a single construction, and counts the optima as partitions of the given vertex set. The exact classification and labeled-vertex count add information not present in the standard upper bound.
